title: What If Every Human Jumped at the Same Moment?

scenes.text: What if every person on Earth jumped at the same moment? You'd expect an earthquake. You'd be wrong.
Pack everyone shoulder to shoulder and we'd fit into about 1,450 square kilometers, a bit bigger than Los Angeles.
All of humanity weighs roughly 500 billion kilograms. Earth weighs about ten trillion times more.
When we leave the ground, Earth recoils. By a tiny fraction of the width of a single atom.
Then we land, and the planet drifts back to where it started. No quake. Nothing a machine could measure.
The only effect would be a long, loud roar of billions of people landing. The planet would barely notice.

description:
What if every human jumped at the same moment?
Humanity is about ten trillion times lighter than Earth, so the planet would move by less than the width of an atom and settle right back.
What should we run through next?
